database_summary: Small mixed-domain SQLite dataset containing (A) alien/person tables (aliens, alien_data, aliens_details, aliens_location) representing individuals and related descriptive/lookups, (B) geopolitical/place/currency tables (cities, cities_countries, cities_currencies, cities_languages) with country/city dimensions, (C) legislative/personnel tables (legislators, legislators_terms, legislation_date_dim) describing legislators and their terms, (D) job postings star-like schema (job_postings_fact, job_company, skills_dim, skills_job_dim) with skill-job bridge, and (E) a few lookup/reference tables. Data includes both current-state descriptive rows and event-like / fact rows (job postings, legislator terms). Several tables share natural keys such as id_bioguide and country_code_2. No explicit foreign key constraints declared in DDL; relationships must be inferred from column names. Joins between fact/bridge tables (skills_job_dim <-> skills_dim, skills_job_dim <-> job_postings_fact via job_id) can multiply rows due to many-to-many mappings and high row counts in bridge tables.

accepted.name: job_postings_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  j.job_id,
  j.company_id,
  c.name AS name,
  c.link AS link,
  c.link_google AS link_google,
  c.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
  j.job_title_short,
  j.job_title,
  j.job_location,
  j.job_via,
  j.job_schedule_type,
  j.job_work_from_home,
  j.search_location,
  j.job_posted_date,
  j.job_no_degree_mention,
  j.job_health_insurance,
  j.job_country,
  j.salary_rate,
  j.salary_year_avg,
  j.salary_hour_avg
FROM job_postings_fact AS j
LEFT JOIN job_company AS c
  ON j.company_id = c.company_id
accepted.description: Denormalized job postings with company metadata and enriched salary measures. Useful as a starting relation for job-level analytics, filtering by company, location, date, or salary. | Use for: Average salary by country or company; Jobs by location or schedule type; Jobs with/without degree mentions; Company-level job counts and salary distributions

accepted.name: legislators_latest_term
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state,
  lt.district,
  lt.class,
  lt.party,
  lt.how,
  lt.url,
  lt.address,
  lt.phone,
  lt.fax,
  lt.contact_form,
  lt.office,
  lt.state_rank,
  lt.rss_url,
  lt.caucus,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_end DESC, lt.term_start DESC) AS term_rank
FROM legislators_terms AS lt
accepted.description: Latest term per legislator (by term_end). One row per id_bioguide with the most recent term record. Useful to get current/stateful legislator attributes derived from terms (e.g., current office, state, party). | Use for: Current office/party/state for a legislator; Filtering to latest term (WHERE term_rank = 1) to join to legislator person table; Counts of incumbents by party or state

accepted.name: legislators_profile
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.id_bioguide,
  l.full_name,
  l.first_name,
  l.last_name,
  l.middle_name,
  l.nickname,
  l.suffix,
  l.other_names_end,
  l.other_names_middle,
  l.other_names_last,
  l.birthday,
  l.gender,
  l.id_bioguide_previous_0,
  l.id_govtrack,
  l.id_icpsr,
  l.id_wikipedia,
  l.id_wikidata,
  l.id_google_entity_id,
  l.id_house_history,
  l.id_house_history_alternate,
  l.id_thomas,
  l.id_cspan,
  l.id_votesmart,
  l.id_lis,
  l.id_ballotpedia,
  l.id_opensecrets,
  l.id_fec_0,
  l.id_fec_1,
  l.id_fec_2,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state AS state,
  lt.district AS district,
  lt.party AS party,
  lt.office AS office
FROM legislators AS l
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT
      lt.*,
      RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_end DESC, lt.term_start DESC) AS term_rank
    FROM legislators_terms AS lt
  ) WHERE term_rank = 1
) AS lt
  ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
accepted.description: Legislator personal profile joined with their latest term to expose person + current-term attributes. One row per legislator (when filtered to latest term). Useful for personnel lists, contact info, and joining to term-based measures. | Use for: List current legislators with contact/party/state information; Join legislators to term-based vote or bill data (if available); Counts by party/state for current incumbents

accepted.name: cities_with_country
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id,
  c.city_name,
  c.latitude,
  c.longitude,
  c.country_code_2,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
  cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
  curr.currency_name AS currency_name,
  curr.currency_code AS currency_code,
  c.capital,
  c.population,
  c.insert_date
FROM cities AS c
LEFT JOIN cities_countries AS cc
  ON lower(c.country_code_2) = lower(cc.country_code_2)
LEFT JOIN cities_currencies AS curr
  ON lower(c.country_code_2) = lower(curr.country_code_2)
accepted.description: City dimension enriched with country attributes (country name, region, sub_region) and currency code where available. One row per city preserving city-level identifiers and country codes. | Use for: City population by country or region; Map city coordinates with region/currency metadata; Identify capital cities and their country attributes

accepted.name: alien_profiles
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.first_name AS first_name,
  a.last_name AS last_name,
  a.email AS email,
  a.gender AS gender,
  a.type AS type,
  a.birth_year AS birth_year,
  ad.age AS age,
  ad.favorite_food AS favorite_food,
  ad.feeding_frequency AS feeding_frequency,
  ad.aggressive AS aggressive,
  al.current_location AS current_location,
  al.state AS state,
  al.country AS country,
  al.occupation AS occupation
FROM aliens AS a
LEFT JOIN alien_data AS ad
  ON a.id = ad.id
LEFT JOIN aliens_location AS al
  ON a.id = al.loc_id
LEFT JOIN aliens_details AS d
  ON a.id = d.detail_id
accepted.description: Combined alien/person profile by joining core aliens with enriched data and location/details where keys align. Preserves identity columns and exposes favorite_food, feeding_frequency, aggressive, occupation, and location attributes. Useful for demographic and behavior analysis of aliens. | Use for: Demographic breakdowns of aliens (age, gender, type); Behavior/feeding patterns by region or occupation; Counts of aggressive aliens or favorite food distributions

accepted.name: cities_population_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  city_name,
  country_code_2,
  population,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code_2 ORDER BY population DESC) AS population_rank
FROM cities
accepted.description: Cities ranked by population within each country_code_2. One row per city with a population_rank to enable top-k per country filtering downstream. | Use for: Top N largest cities by country; Rank-based city selections for mapping or reporting; Comparing city populations within a country

accepted.name: job_postings_salary_agg_by_country
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_country,
  COUNT(job_id) AS job_posting_count,
  AVG(salary_year_avg) AS avg_salary_year,
  AVG(salary_hour_avg) AS avg_salary_hour
FROM job_postings_fact
GROUP BY job_country
accepted.description: Aggregated salary measures per job_country: count of postings and average salary (year/hour). Useful for country-level salary comparisons and trend baselines. | Use for: Average salary by country; Number of job postings per country; Compare hourly vs yearly salary averages across countries

accepted.name: skills_demand_by_job
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.skill_id,
  s.skills,
  s.type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT j.job_id) AS jobs_with_skill,
  COUNT(j.job_id) AS skill_job_mappings
FROM skills_dim AS s
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim AS j
  ON s.skill_id = j.skill_id
GROUP BY s.skill_id, s.skills, s.type
accepted.description: Counts of distinct jobs and occurrences per skill. One row per skill (skill_id) with measures for number of jobs that reference the skill and total mappings. | Use for: Most in-demand skills by job count; Skill popularity and density across job postings; Skill type rollups
